boards.title: Your First Weekend at San Jose State University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key first-weekend sequence that moves from campus orientation and public art to recreation, study, and nearby San José culture.

cards.entity_name: San José State University Main Campus
cards.title: Start with the main-campus map
cards.subtitle: One Washington Square
cards.notes: Open the official interactive map before setting out, then use it to locate buildings, services, and amenities as you get your bearings.
cards.short_summary: A practical first stop for navigating the 88-acre downtown campus.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU’s official main-campus page provides an interactive map and identifies the campus as 88 acres in downtown San José.
cards.access_notes: Use the university’s interactive map for current route and building details.

cards.title: See Victory Salute on Tower Lawn
cards.subtitle: Tower Lawn, SJSU
cards.notes: Pause at the monument and read its context: it depicts SJSU alumni Tommie Smith and John Carlos during their 1968 Olympic protest.
cards.short_summary: A documented public-art stop centered on SJSU alumni and civil-rights history.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU identifies Victory Salute as a 2005 monument by Rigo 23 on Tower Lawn depicting alumni Tommie Smith and John Carlos.
cards.source_title: Victory Salute | Public Art as Resistance in San Jose
cards.access_notes: Outdoor monument; consult the campus map for its precise location.

cards.title: Orient yourself at Tower Hall
cards.subtitle: SJSU main campus
cards.notes: Use the map-listed landmark as a visual checkpoint, then continue toward nearby campus destinations at a comfortable walking pace.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable named campus landmark for orienting a first walk.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU’s official campus map lists Tower Hall as a main-campus building.
cards.access_notes: Check the current campus map for access and route information.

cards.entity_name: Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Library
cards.title: Make a library base camp
cards.subtitle: 150 E. San Fernando St.
cards.notes: Find a study seat, browse the public-library side, or use the building as a meeting point before the next campus activity.
cards.short_summary: A shared City of San José and SJSU library at the campus edge.
cards.evidence_claim: San José Public Library describes King Library as a partnership between the City of San José and San José State University.
cards.source_title: King Library | San Jose Public Library
cards.access_notes: The library publishes current daily hours; enrolled SJSU students may have extended study access.

cards.title: Get oriented in the Student Union
cards.subtitle: SJSU main campus
cards.notes: Use the building directory to locate services, dining options, resource centers, and the day’s practical campus destinations in one place.
cards.short_summary: A campus hub with maps, directories, services, and dining locations.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Union’s official page provides building maps and a directory for departments, services, dining options, and resource centers.
cards.access_notes: Check the Student Union’s official hours page before visiting.

cards.title: Try the SJSU Bowling Center
cards.subtitle: Diaz Compean Student Union
cards.notes: Check the center’s current schedule, then plan a casual game or billiards session with new classmates during an available window.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus recreation option with separately published operating hours.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU’s Student Union publishes regular operating hours for its Bowling Center.
cards.source_title: Hours | Student Union, Inc. at SJSU
cards.access_notes: The official hours page lists Bowling Center hours; confirm schedules and activity availability before arrival.

cards.title: Move at the SRAC
cards.subtitle: 324 Paseo de San Carlos
cards.notes: Choose an activity that fits your comfort level, such as a pickup game, cycling class, climbing wall, or pool-side recreation.
cards.short_summary: A named campus recreation facility with multiple activity options.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU says the Spartan Recreation and Aquatic Center offers cycling classes, a rock-climbing wall, pickup games, and recreation-pool access.
cards.source_title: Spartan Recreation | Student Union, Inc. at SJSU
cards.access_notes: Access and program availability can vary; review current Spartan Recreation information before visiting.

cards.title: Take a quiet lap by the Spartan Rose Garden
cards.subtitle: SJSU main campus
cards.notes: Use the official map to find this named point of interest, then take a short outdoor reset before heading toward downtown.
cards.short_summary: A named campus point of interest for an outdoor pause.
cards.evidence_claim: SJSU’s official campus map identifies the Spartan Rose Garden as a point of interest.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access conditions may change; use the current campus map and follow posted guidance.

cards.title: Visit the San José Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: 110 South Market Street, downtown San José
cards.notes: Bring a valid college ID and check the current exhibitions and hours before walking over for an afternoon of contemporary art.
cards.short_summary: A downtown art museum that offers free individual admission to college students with valid ID.
cards.evidence_claim: San José Museum of Art states that college students with valid ID receive free individual admission and lists its downtown address.
cards.source_title: Visit | San José Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Bring valid college ID for the stated free student admission; verify current exhibition hours before going.

cards.title: End with a walk through History Park
cards.subtitle: Kelley Park, San José
cards.notes: Set aside daylight time to walk the 14-acre grounds, then check whether historic buildings are open during your visit.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor history site with original and reconstructed San José buildings and landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: History San José describes History Park as a 14-acre town-like assemblage of original and reconstructed homes, businesses, and landmarks.
cards.access_notes: History Park posts daily park hours and separate historic-building hours; verify both before traveling.
